target.title: Add secure bridge artifact transfer
target.body:
## Summary

- transfer ChatGPT-generated files from a browser bridge host back to the client through a token-protected pull endpoint
- advertise protocol support and size limits through `/health` capability negotiation
- sanitize filenames and verify byte count, SHA-256, and ZIP structure before publishing client-local artifacts
- serialize same-name artifact allocation so concurrent bridge events cannot overwrite or deduplicate files
- preserve text responses and provide a manual-copy fallback for mixed-version or failed transfers
- expose validation and transfer metadata in stored sessions and bridge diagnostics

## Security

The NDJSON result contains only redacted descriptors. It does not expose host filesystem paths, ChatGPT cookies, bridge credentials, signed download URLs, or host-only warnings. The host registers only real files beneath Oracle session artifact directories. Artifact fetches reuse the existing bridge bearer token, reject malformed identifiers, stream through a fixed byte limit, and expire from the host registry after a bounded TTL.

## Validation

- exact candidate: `66b02f3c0a5e99d8b4f90b70804369fe56e796f3`
- `pnpm run check`
- `pnpm run build`
- `pnpm run docs:check && pnpm run docs:site`
- focused bridge/browser tests: 26 passed
- full unit suite: 1,345 passed, 43 skipped
- full-branch autoreview: clean after fixing a same-name parallel-transfer race
- full CI: passed on Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, and GitGuardian ([run](https://github.com/steipete/oracle/actions/runs/28499532017))
- contributor smoke on the earlier head transferred a generated ZIP from a live Windows browser host to a Linux client with matching SHA-256 and valid ZIP structure; exact-head cross-host rerun remains required before merge
